# Doefin brand: overview

How Doefin looks and how it writes, on the website, in the app, on X and LinkedIn, in email and in decks. The writing matters most. If you read one file, read `voice.md`.

## Doefin in one line

**Markets for Bitcoin mining difficulty.**

When there is room for more: Doefin lets professional investors take positions on Bitcoin mining difficulty. Each market asks one question: will difficulty be at or above a set level at a set block? Markets settle from public Bitcoin network data.

Describe Doefin in these plain words. Don't call it "hashrate derivatives" or a "prediction market".

Company line for footers, documents and decks: Doefin, Port Louis, Mauritius.

## Who we write for

Miners and the people who finance them, and funds and trading desks. All of them are professional investors. They know mining and check the maths. They stop reading at the first line of hype. We never write for retail readers.

## The short version

- `ink` and white do most of the work. Doefin Blue marks the one thing to look at.
- Flat colour. No gradients, glows or frosted glass.
- Manrope for everything, with figures that line up in columns.
- Numbers come with their unit, and with a date and a source whenever they can change.
- Short sentences and real numbers. Write it the way you would say it to a miner on the phone.
- Use the logo files as they are. Never redraw, stretch or recolour them.

## Before anything goes out

- Does the first line get straight to the subject?
- Does every number that can change have a date and a source?
- Would you say it this way to a miner on the phone?
- Did it pass the copy checker (`tools/check_copy.py`)?
- Is it free of return figures, promises and anything aimed at retail?
- If it is public and about Doefin or its markets, has Raffaella Tenconi approved it in writing? That includes a single post.
